properties.title: Chronus — Hardware Product, Contract & API Lock

content: Locked identity: hardware-aware enterprise acceleration and truthful execution evidence, scoped to Chronus hardware capabilities. This record does not rename packages. Naming correction from current source review: the publication catalog distinguishes hyba-chronos-mathematics, hyba-chronos-one-igpu, hyba-chronus-igpu and planned hyba-chronus-tensor. Chronos must not be treated as a blanket spelling alias for Chronus. The earlier alias assumption is withdrawn. Map each distribution to its actual API/version and evidence before publication; the mathematics package needs its own scoped contract rather than inheriting this hardware charter. Whole-System Release Decision — Production & Publication. Status: authority baseline documented; callable/transport mapping and target hardware qualification open. ## Owned authority Device probing and fingerprinting, scheduling, memory/transfer handling, eligible CPU/iGPU/GPU execution, invariant verification and evidence of where work actually ran. Kellogg owns tensor mathematics/artifact semantics. Ovid owns versioned fold/materialise; Theseus owns durable custody. Chronus must not change canonical digests or correctness to obtain throughput. ## Contract and API inventory | Surface | Required obligation | | --- | --- | | Capability manifest | Identify actual device/backend and limits; unknown hardware facts remain null, not guessed from vendor marketing | | Execution request | Bind operation, input shape/dtype, resource limits, required backend/device, exactness and permitted fallback policy | | Execution result | Identify actual execution backend/device, output identity, transfer and compute evidence, refusal/degradation state | | Device-required mode | Fail closed when the requested device/path is unavailable; no silent host fallback | | Host mode | Label host execution honestly, including historical kellogg-host label where applicable | Historical source surfaces include chronus.phi_gpu, chronus.v33 and Kellogg-backed MPS/TT/MPO integration. A separate tensor control API is recorded in the production closeout; its routes must not be assumed to be identical to every Chronus package API. Exact exports, schemas and authentication bindings remain to be reconciled at a pinned commit. A child adapter or micro-tether does not create another physical iGPU. Dated topology references are not device measurements. Do not claim FP64 or folded-native support merely from scheduling eligibility. ## Non-mining acceptance requirement Run a representative enterprise tensor operation against a CPU/reference baseline; confirm output/error bounds, requested-device refusal, actual device identity and complete transfer/compute timing. Include unavailable-device and resource-exhaustion cases. No new benchmark execution is asserted. ## Mining boundary Optional mining execution remains subordinate to canonical hashing, target and pool authorities. Scheduling estimates and algebraic dimensions are not hashes per second or accepted shares. ## Customer schedule Specify supported hardware/software matrix, operation classes, fallback policy and customer prerequisites. Do not promise universal GPU acceleration or vendor-specific bandwidth absent measurement. Fees, support/SLA and license are separate approved commercial terms. ## Source traceability - Converge July tensor capabilities into Kellogg and close Chronus GPU gaps - feat(aethel): Chronus·Theseus·Ovid enterprise custody substrate - Production & Publication Closeout — Evidence and Gates - HYBA — Enterprise Product Lock Register
